source.extractionNote: Re-extracted 2026-10-21 after the designer's update. All five sets read in full (every variant, depth 12) and both metadata frames parsed; set and frame ids are unchanged. Nested instances were then read per variant for the props the deltas don't see: the Icon Button Shape inside the master (follows rounded), the Caret Indicator Open/Direction inside each item (follows Open; Direction is overridden in the selectable item), and the Selected mark's glyph. The only structural change since 2026-10-20 is the title text style on both header sets: title/large → title/medium, which shortens the plain header's hug height (see issues). Master, item sets, nested instance props, token bindings other than the title's, and all metadata text are unchanged. The page has two metadata frames, one for Accordion and one for Accordion Item; the item frame documents the four private sets as one logical row component.

summary: A vertically stacked list of disclosure rows sharing one container, for a page that has more sections than it has room to show at once. Selectable decides whether rows can be ticked as well as opened, and In Card decides whether the list reads as a bounded object. The rows themselves are separate components with their own frames.

controls: items slot (which of the two slots)

intent.true: Rows carry a leading control and can be ticked, so the list doubles as a chooser. Reach for it when someone has to mark items, not merely read them. It is the same row component either way, with the selection turned on.
intent.false: Rows disclose content only, with the caret trailing the title. The right choice for content reveal, an FAQ or a settings group where nothing is being chosen.

Match the contour of the surface the list sits on rather than deciding per instance. Only the outer container responds, so on a long list the difference shows at the first and last rows and nowhere else.
intent.true: The rounded pairing, for surfaces built from rounded controls. The nested row buttons inherits the rounding.
Treat the list as one bounded object, set apart from what surrounds it. This also turns the row dividers on, so the choice governs the internal rhythm as much as the outer edge.
intent.false: Let the list sit directly on the page and take its separation from the surrounding layout. Dividers disappears with the outline, so rows run together and the container has to supply the breathing room.

items.expects: Accordion Item (selectable or not, matching selectable)
items.note: Figma holds two slot properties, one per Selectable value; preferred content is _Accordion Item Selectable and _Accordion Item respectively. The metadata states that in code this is a single content slot.

internalVariations.intent: No property on this set opens a row. Open sits on the nested header and reads false in all eight variants, so the set documents the collapsed list only. Only one item can have the open state at a time.
internalVariations.note: Open is in fact a variant of the nested item, not the header (see issues). In code it becomes per-item open state owned by the Accordion.

internalVariations.intent: Selected and hover live on the nested header; neither the item nor the Accordion surfaces them.
Title is a text property on the header set only; it is set by overriding the nested instance.

contentInputs.sample: Four rows titled "Heading", all closed: one fixed row, two in the slot, one fixed row

contentInputs.note: The row's Content Slot is empty by default and declares no preferred content.

anatomy.role: The outer frame. It owns the border, the corner radius and the vertical stacking, and carries no fill of its own.

measured._note: In Card=true; In Card=false measures 379×224Px (no stroke)

anatomy.role: The first and last rows, placed directly in the variant rather than in the slot. They are not swappable content.
The middle region a consumer fills with rows. Which of the two slots is present follows the Selectable axis.
The first and last rows, placed directly in the variant rather than in the slot. They are not swappable content.
anatomy.note: Figma-only split per the metadata: in code every row is slot content and the last row always has its divider off.

variants._note: rounded=true also switches the nested Icon Button (leading control of selectable rows) from Shape=sharp to Shape=rounded; that is the 'nested row buttons inherit the rounding' the metadata describes. Non-selectable rows have no button, so rounded affects only the container there. measured.* cells are observations, not tokens.

subcomponents.name: Accordion Item
subcomponents.summary: One row of an Accordion, holding a title, a disclosure control, and the content it reveals. Selectable decides whether the row also carries a selection, which changes the controls it offers and how a tap is divided between them. Open, the title, the divider and the content behave the same either way.

intent.true: The row carries a selection as well as disclosure. A leading control takes the open and close and the rest of the row takes the selection, so the two actions never share a target.
intent.false: Disclosure only. The whole row is a single target that opens and closes it, and the caret trails the title instead of leading.

selectable.note: Not a Figma property: two component sets. The item metadata says they are one component with a Selectable variant.

intent.true: Expanded, with the content sitting below the title and the caret rotated to match.
A rule closing the row off from the next one.
intent.false: No rule. Which rows carry one is decided by the Accordion placing them, not by the row itself.

title.intent: The row's label. Name the section it opens, because the caret says that a row opens but never what is inside it.

intent.false: Not chosen. It only carries meaning while Selectable is on, because nothing else offers a way to choose.
intent.true: Chosen. A mark trails the title and the heading gives up the width it needs.

intent.hover: Pointer over the row. Only the background answers, so hover is the weakest of the signals this row gives.

anatomy.role: The frame holding the header and, when open, the content beneath it.
The title with its disclosure control. The control leads when Selectable is on and trails when it is off.

measured._note: Both header kinds measure 56Px inside the item: the plain header is pinned to a fixed 56Px (it hugs to 52Px on its own since the title/medium change), the selectable one hugs to 56Px. See issues.

anatomy.role: What the row reveals when open, with a rule closing it off from the next row.

variants._note: The caret is a nested Caret Indicator whose Open variant the item sets to match its own. The selectable item also overrides the caret's Direction to horizontal, giving chevron-right → expand-more; the non-selectable item keeps Direction=vertical, giving expand-more → expand-less. In Figma both are glyph swaps; by owner decision code rotates one glyph instead (see ownerDecisions).

measured._note: Standalone set measurements. The plain header was 56Px tall while the title was title/large; with title/medium it hugs to 52Px, and the item pins it back to a fixed 56Px.

anatomy.refVariant: Size=medium, Shape=sharp (rounded when Accordion rounded=true), Flavour=subtle, State=default, Disabled=false
anatomy.role: An Icon Button carrying the caret. It owns the open and close, runs its own interaction states, and takes its shape from the Accordion around it.
anatomy.inCode: Owner decision: one glyph (chevron-right) rotated 90deg clockwise when open, animated on animations/spring, rather than swapping to expand-more.

anatomy.role: A Caret Indicator trailing the title, rotating with the open state. It is not a control of its own, because the whole row is the target.
anatomy.inCode: Owner decision: one glyph (expand-more) rotated 180deg when open, animated on animations/spring, rather than swapping to expand-less.

anatomy.role: A framed check icon at the trailing edge. It reports the selection rather than offering it, since the row body is what toggles it.

dependencies.name: Icon
dependencies.usedAs: selection mark (Framed=true), and inside Caret Indicator

dependencies.name: Caret Indicator
dependencies.note: Lives on the Navigation Rail page; specced in specs/navigation-rail (subcomponents › Caret Indicator). In code it reduces to a glyph chosen by open state and direction.

viaDependencies: stroke/base (Icon Button's own bindings, recorded on the instance)
tokens._note: All 21 bound variable names (including the five title/medium/* properties of the title/medium text style, which replace title/large/*) resolve in tokens/base. animations/spring is not bound in Figma; it is named by owner decision for the caret rotation and the panel height, and resolves in tokens/base/size. All four glyphs are in packages/icons/codepoints.json, not retired, and absent from inventory.json's rejected list.
motion: animations/spring (owner decision; not bound in Figma, which models no motion)

accordion.whatChanges: The set declares no state axis of its own. Nothing about the container changes on hover, focus or press.
Handled inside the row components and documented in their frames. The container does not repaint.

item.whatChanges: The resting row, with nothing emphasised.
The background lifts. The title, the caret and any selection mark all hold, so the background carries the whole change.
The content appears below the title and the caret rotates to point at it. The row grows to fit whatever the content needs.

item.trigger: Selected set to true, while Selectable is on
item.whatChanges: A mark appears at the trailing edge and the heading narrows to make room for it.

accordion.description: Figma stores no timing, and no expand or collapse transition is authored. The height change that opening a row implies is not modelled.

No property on this set opens a row. Open sits on the nested header and reads false in all eight variants, so the set documents the collapsed list only. Only one item can have the open state at a time.

Selectable switches the interaction model as well as the look. Without it the whole header toggles the row open. With it, the leading icon button takes the open and close and the rest of the header takes the selection.

item.description: No transition is defined. Opening a row is the content appearing and the caret rotating, with nothing specified in between.

Without Selectable the whole row is one target that opens and closes it. With Selectable the leading control takes the open and close and the rest of the row takes the selection, so the two actions never share a target.
Nothing links one row's selection to another. Whether one row or many may be chosen is decided where the rows are placed.

accordion.type: slot, present when Selectable is true
accordion.description: Takes Accordion Item rows with Selectable on, one per row. This is the only part of the list a consumer adds to. Figma holds two slots, one per Selectable value, so the row content can stay locked in each. In code it is a single content slot.

accordion.type: slot, present when Selectable is false
accordion.description: The same role for the non-selectable rows. Only one of the two slots exists in any given variant, so the Selectable choice decides which one is available. This is a Figma only implementation, in code both slots are available as a single content slot.

The row above the slot and the row below it are placed instances rather than slot content. Reordering or removing them means detaching, and the last one is where the divider is deliberately switched off. The are static element in Figma only, in code the last element will always have the divider turned off

item.description: Plain text, defaulting to Heading. The only text the row takes.

item.type: slot, present when Open is true
item.description: Holds whatever the row reveals. It takes any content and is what sets the row's open height.

item.type: nested, present when Selectable is on
item.description: An Icon Button carrying the caret. It owns the open and close, runs its own interaction states, and takes its shape from the Accordion around it.

item.type: nested, present when Selectable is off
item.description: A Caret Indicator trailing the title, rotating with the open state. It is not a control of its own, because the whole row is the target.

item.type: nested, present when Selected is true
item.description: A framed check icon at the trailing edge. It reports the selection rather than offering it, since the row body is what toggles it.

Selectable and non-selectable rows are built as two component sets so the slot content can stay locked in each. They are one component with a Selectable variant, and the split carries no meaning beyond authoring.

do: Pick Selectable before filling the slot. Changing it later swaps the row component and drops the titles already entered.
Keep In Card consistent across sibling lists on one screen. It governs the dividers as well as the border, so a mixed pair reads as two different components.
dont: Don't expect to open a row from the Accordion instance. Open lives on the nested header and is not surfaced here.
Don't treat the first and last rows as slot content. They are fixed instances, and the last one has its divider deliberately turned off.

do: Write titles that name the section. The caret says that a row opens, the title has to say what is inside it.
Decide Selectable once for a whole list. A row that selects sitting next to rows that only open reads as two different controls.
dont: Don't put a second control inside a non-selectable row. The whole row is one target, so anything else competes with it.
Don't use Selected without Selectable. The mark appears with no control behind it to change it.

accordion: No focus state is modelled anywhere in the set, so the keyboard path through the rows has to be built in code.
The caret is the only sign that a row expands. Expose expanded and collapsed as real state rather than leaving it to the glyph.
With In Card false there is no border and no divider, so nothing separates the rows until one is hovered. Check the list still reads as a list at rest.
Titles use title/large at 20px, which is heading sized. On a screen with real headings the hierarchy needs checking.
Opening a row reveals content that was not previously in the reading order. That insertion has to be announced.
item: Without Selectable the whole row is one control. It needs a single focusable target carrying its expanded state.
With Selectable there are two targets, the leading control for open and close and the rest of the row for selection. Each needs its own name, or one of the two actions cannot be reached.
The caret's rotation is the only sign that a row is open. Expanded and collapsed have to be exposed in the markup rather than left to the glyph.
Selection shows as a trailing mark. It needs a real selected state alongside it.
Hover changes the background and nothing else, so anyone not using a pointer gets no equivalent signal.
The title is set at 20px, which is heading sized. On a screen carrying real headings the hierarchy needs checking.

accordion.description: Width fills available space or restricted as needed. Height always hugs the rows.
A 1px inside stroke bound to border/default when In Card is true. No stroke at all when it is false.
radius/lg on all four corners when rounded is true. When false the radius is a literal 0.
The container carries no fill. Every surface colour in the list comes from the row components.
Vertical, zero padding, and the gap bound to space/none so rows butt directly against each other.
With In Card true, Show Divider is on for every row except the last. With In Card false it is off on all of them. The value is baked into each instance and is not exposed.
56 per row, rising to 57 wherever a divider is switched on.

item.description: Fills its container. The header is 56 tall and a row carrying its divider is 57. Open rows grow to whatever the content needs.
space/lg on all four sides of the header without Selectable, and space/sm with it, because the leading control is taller than the title.
space/sm between the title and the caret without Selectable, space/xs between the control, the title and the mark with it.
interactive/ghost/background/default at rest and interactive/ghost/background/hover on hover. No border and no corner radius.
title/large, IBM Plex Sans Medium 20 over a 24px line, in foreground/primary.
Caret Indicator at Size=medium, 20 square, trailing the title when Selectable is off.
Icon Button at Size=medium, 40 square, Flavour=subtle, leading the title when Selectable is on.
A framed Icon at 40 square on the trailing edge, present only while Selected is true.
A 1px horizontal rule beneath the row, adding 1 to its height when shown.

ownerDecisions.decision: The caret rotates one glyph with animation rather than swapping glyphs.
ownerDecisions.appliesTo: the plain row's trailing caret (expand-more, rotated 180deg when open) and the selectable row's leading-control glyph (chevron-right, rotated 90deg clockwise when open)
ownerDecisions.figma: Figma still swaps glyphs through Caret Indicator's Open variant; the decision overrides that in code.

ownerDecisions.decision: Motion that matches Switch uses the animations/spring token (--animations-spring).
ownerDecisions.appliesTo: the caret rotation and the content panel's height change on open and close; no transition under prefers-reduced-motion
ownerDecisions.figma: Figma models no motion on this page; the metadata says no transition is authored.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: The title now uses the title/medium text style on both header sets (all five font properties bound to title/medium/*); it was title/large. The metadata has not caught up: Item Layout & Theming still reads 'title/large, IBM Plex Sans Medium 20 over a 24px line', and both Accessibility lists still say the title is 'title/large at 20px' / 'set at 20px, which is heading sized'. title/medium resolves to 16px over a 20px line in every typography mode, so the heading-size concern no longer holds as written; what remains is that the title is still the row's only label, so whether it is marked up as a heading (and at which level) is a page-hierarchy decision for code. Owner to update the three metadata lines; they are kept verbatim here.

Plain header height. With title/large the plain header hugged to 56Px (space/lg + 24Px line + space/lg), the same as the selectable header (space/sm + control/md + space/sm). With title/medium it hugs to 52Px standalone, but _Accordion Item pins its nested plain header to a fixed 56Px with no token bound, so rows still measure 56Px (57Px with a divider) as the metadata's 'Row height' says. Code keeps 56 by giving the plain trigger a min-height of control/md + 2 × space/sm, so plain and selectable rows match. Owner decision: confirm 56 is intended for plain rows (and bind or document it), or let them hug to 52.
Accordion root stroke width is a raw 1px in all four In Card=true variants; only its colour is bound (border/default). stroke/thin exists and is what the row Divider uses.
Accordion metadata says 'Open sits on the nested header'. Open is a variant of the nested Accordion Item (_Accordion Item / _Accordion Item Selectable); neither header set has an Open property.
Accordion Layout & Theming says width is 'Fill/Flexible'; the root is fixed width in all eight variants (measured 381Px with In Card, 379Px without). Treat width as owned by the container in code.

The Accordion Item metadata lists Selectable, Open, Selected, State, Title and Show Divider as item properties. On the item sets only Open, Show Divider and Content Slot exist; Selected, State and Title live on the nested header sets and are not surfaced; Selectable is the choice between two sets. Intended as one logical component, so the spec models it that way.

Metadata describes the caret as rotating. In Figma it is a glyph swap through Caret Indicator's Open variant: expand-more → expand-less (plain rows), chevron-right → expand-more (selectable rows, where the item overrides the caret's Direction to horizontal). The standalone _Accordion Header Selectable set pins Direction=vertical, so on its own it shows expand-more while closed, which disagrees with how the item uses it. Decide one convention in code. Resolved by owner decision (see ownerDecisions): code rotates one glyph with animation; Figma has not been redrawn to match.

'Only one item can have the open state at a time' is stated only in Accordion's Behavior row; nothing in Figma models it, and the item metadata is silent. Single-expand is the intent; whether multiple-open is ever allowed is a code decision.
The Content Slot hugs horizontally rather than filling, while the item metadata says the row fills its container. Content would not stretch to the row width; fill is the evident intent.

No focus, pressed or disabled state anywhere (container, rows or headers); hover is the only state. No motion is authored; code animates the caret and panel on animations/spring by owner decision. Both are stated as intentionally absent in the metadata.
Root corner radius is bound to radius/lg only when rounded=true; rounded=false is an unbound 0, which the metadata states explicitly.
Open, Selected, hover and Title are reachable only by overriding nested instances. In code, open and selected become per-item state owned by the Accordion; title becomes item content.

First and last rows sit outside the slot as fixed instances, and Figma has two slot properties (one per Selectable). Both are Figma-only per the metadata: in code there is one list of items, and the last item never shows a divider.
Title text has no truncation or line limit and hugs its width; long-title behaviour isn't specified.

Caret Indicator lives on the Navigation Rail page and is specced in specs/navigation-rail (subcomponents › Caret Indicator). It reduces to a glyph (rounded family, currentColor) picked by open state and direction.
No component-set descriptions on any of the five sets.
Verbatim copy keeps the authored typos ('The nested row buttons inherits', 'Dividers disappears', 'The are static element').
